title: Locus coeruleus regulation of hippocampal network reset during learning
text:
Attention and memory systems closely interact to ensure we encode the things that matter. In this proposal, we
will test whether the brain systems that control attention and arousal affect memory centers by driving changes
in neural activity when the focus of attention shifts, a process that is essential for cognitive and behavioral
flexibility. By studying the gate that controls transitions between neural representations, we hope to provide a
new lens through which to understand the comorbid attention and memory deficits seen across psychiatric and
neurological conditions.

title: Data Science for Decision Support in the HIV Care Cascade
text:
Retention in care and viral suppression via antiretroviral therapy are critical for continuing
progress toward global elimination of HIV. This proposal develops and evaluates data-driven
clinical decision support tools that are designed to maximize retention and viral suppression by
identifying patients who will benefit from proactive support and other interventions. The tools
utilize data from electronic health records and are customized to low- and middle-income country
settings; successful implementation will maximize patient engagement in care, further reduce HIV
incidence, and enable continued progress toward worldwide elimination of HIV.

title: Microcircuit mechanisms behind the distributed cortical contributions to working memory
text:
Working memory, or the ability to remember and manipulate information without sensory input, is central to
cognitive behavior, but we still do not understand how distributed cortical regions distinctly contribute to this
ability. We will combine cutting-edge methods in computational neuroscience, genetics, complex behavior in
virtual reality, and simultaneous optical recording and perturbation of neural activity, to understand how
microcircuits in two areas of the mouse cerebral hold information on different timescales. Our work has important
implications for normal aging, autism, and schizophrenia, all of which have been associated with alterations in
both working memory and activity timescales across the human cortex.

title: Mechanisms of myocarditis and progressive cardiac fibrosis in chronic Trypanosoma cruzi infection.
text:
Chronic infection with Trypanosoma cruzi results in chronic inflammation and progressive cardiac fibrosis, known
as Chronic Chagasic Cardiomyopathy. Our goal is to better define the mechanisms of inflammation and fibrosis
to identify host specific targets for intervention. Ultimately, this approach will identify therapies that can be used
in an integrated, multimodal treatment strategy to preserve cardiac health and improve clinical outcomes for
patients with CCC.

title: Investigating the Regulatory Logic Underlying Meningeal Development and Tumorigenesis
text:
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
Cranial neural crest cells are critical for the formation of diverse craniofacial structures including bones, cartilage,
and meninges. Defects in meningeal development lead to improper skull development whereas its uncontrolled
proliferation can lead to tumors called meningiomas. The proposed aims will demonstrate gene networks
involved in meningeal development and tumorigenesis, providing significant and novel avenues for translational
approaches to treat skull defects and meningiomas.

title: High-throughput spatial proteomics in pulmonary research with FLASH multiplex imaging
text:
Understanding the complex functions of normal cellular processes at a molecular level,
particularly how individual cells and their microenvironment interact over time and space, will
provide new insights into the cellular mechanisms disrupted in fibrotic diseases. In this project,
we will develop AFLEX, the first automated subcellular spatial proteomics platform technology
that is capable of multiplexed data generation on the scale of minutes versus hours, and validate
its applicability in healthy and fibrotic formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded human lung tissue. This
development is crucial for advancing public health as it aims to transform the way we identify,
treat, and prevent fibrotic diseases, opening new horizons in biomarker discovery and
therapeutics.

title: Data Sciences Core
text: DATA SCIENCES CORE ABSTRACT The Data Sciences Core will facilitate Center member research by employing environmental health-related data resources and data science approaches. The core will be led by EDGE investigators experienced in data science methods for omics, exposure sciences, and clinical and epidemiological studies, who will provide expert advice and consultations for Center members in the areas of bioinformatics, biostatistics, geospatial and other analytical fields, including machine learning and artificial intelligence ML/AI methods. Through workshops, the Core will expand awareness and use of data practices that adhere to FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship. The Core will also maintain reproducible analytical pipelines that can be reused across multiple investigator studies. The Data Sciences Core will also facilitate center members’ access to a variety of resources, including data from world-class epidemiological studies, as well as high-performance computing resources. The Data Sciences Core will be tightly integrated with other center activities, including involvement from the Community Engagement Core on data report-back and data ownership and sharing aspects of a Model Community Partnership Agreement for community-engaged research; consultations for Early Career Enhancement Investigators and pilot grant investigators; presentations at the center’s annual symposium; and tracking of resource use and outcomes via the Center’s evaluation process.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis and periodontal disease
text:
Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) arises from aging-associated acquired mutations in
hematopoietic stem cells that expand in the bone marrow giving rise to white blood cells with increased
inflammatory activity. This project investigates the hypothesis that CHIP driven by DNMT3A mutations increases
the severity of periodontal disease. If confirmed, this knowledge has medical significance: screening of the
elderly for CHIP may identify individuals with increased risk for periodontal disease and such patients may benefit
from preventive treatments aiming to block the aberrant expansion of CHIP mutant clones and their harmful
impact on periodontal disease.

title: Distinguishing α-Synuclein S129 Phosphorylation in Health and Lewy Body Dementia
text:
The proposed research is important to public health because it focuses on α-synuclein (αS), a central
protein implicated in Parkinson’s disease (PD), PD with dementia (PDD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and
Alzheimer’s disease (AD). The applicants have developed a unique set of experimental approaches to
distinguish normal and abnormal Serine129 phosphorylation in αS since this post-translational modification is a
principal component of “Lewy bodies”, pathological αS deposits in diseased brains. Therefore, the proposed
research is relevant to NIA’s “AD/ADRD” mission of seeking fundamental knowledge to reduce the burden of PD,
PDD, DLB, and AD patients.

title: NANO-PAVE: A Nanopore-Based Method for AAV Capsid Quality Assessment
text:
This project aims to develop NANO-PAVE, a nanopore-based method for accurately assessing the quality of
adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids used in gene therapy. By enabling precise, single-particle analysis of
capsid load and genome content, NANO-PAVE addresses critical limitations of current quality control methods.
Successful implementation will enhance the safety, efficacy, and consistency of AAV-based therapeutics,
benefiting patients receiving gene therapy and supporting broader adoption of the technology in both academic
and industrial settings, thereby advancing the reliability of gene therapy and promoting public health.

title: Single-Cell Multi-omics to Link Clonal Mosaicism (CM) Genotypes with Chromatin, Epigenomic, Transcriptomic and Protein Phenotypes
text:
DNA mutations drive the outgrowth of small populations of cells in normal tissue, years before clinical diagnosis
of cancer. However, how such mutations change cellular behavior to provide them with a competitive growth
advantage over adjacent cells remains poorly understood. To address this gap in knowledge, we propose to
apply and develop novel single-cell sequencing technologies to study the mechanisms underlying growth
advantage in normal tissues.

title: Diversifying Tuberculosis Vaccine Pipeline with Multivalent Subunit Particle Vaccines
text:
We have developed the SNAP-TB vaccine based a clinically validated liposome nanoparticle platform that
simultaneously binds, displays, and adjuvants three recombinant Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens to induce
strong protective immunity against tuberculosis. We will ready SNAP-TB for human translation by advancing the
manufacturability of SNAP-TB and assessing short-term and long-term protection against multiple
Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains in murine and guinea pig models.

title: Discovery of Natural Products and Natural Product Derivatives as Inhibitors of KLK6 to Prevent the Progression of Preneoplastic Ductal Pancreatic Cancer
text:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), the most common form of pancreatic cancer, is one of the most
lethal diseases in the United States with a five-year survival rate of only 12%, largely due to the late-stage
diagnosis of advanced incurable disease that is impervious to existing chemotherapies. Early detection,
prevention, and intervention strategies are crucial in improving patient outcomes; however, such prevention
strategies remain understudied. To address this gap, we aim to conduct the fundamental research which will
underpin the development of future preventive therapeutics by developing assays to identify natural products,
and derivatives thereof, that have efficacy in intercepting progression from pre-invasive to invasive cancer.

title: Self-amplifying mRNA-based vaccines to elicit VRC01-class bnAbs
text:
The development of a globally effective HIV-1 vaccine will require the elicitation of broadly
neutralizing antibody responses. As such, our proposed studies in this IPCAVD grant are highly
relevant to the development of such a vaccine, as we aim to evaluate in humans self-amplifying
mRNA vaccines that express two HIV-1 Env-derived protein immunogens that can initiate the
maturation of VRC01-class broadly neutralizing antibodies.

title: Detecting prostate cancer aggressiveness using photoacoustic chemical imaging with photoacoustic spectral analysis
text:
Proposed here is a novel laser and ultrasound based imaging platform which, by working together with nano-
size particles carrying functional dyes, may allow not only sensitive detection of prostate cancer but also accurate
differentiation between aggressive and non-aggressive tumors. In this research on clinically relevant mouse
models of prostate cancer, we will test the performance of this imaging technology to pave its road toward
potential clinical translation. In this future, this imaging technology could be integrated into the current standard
clinic procedure, i.e. trans-rectal ultrasound guided needle biopsy, to largely enhance the accuracy in prostate
cancer diagnosis.

title: Caenorhabditis Intervention Testing Program at Oregon
text:
This project will identify pharmacological interventions that improve the length of life and/or the quality of aging
in a simple animal model that shares many hallmark features of aging in humans. Data obtained at three assay
sites by rigorously testing a genetically diverse test set is anticipated to identify chemical treatments with high
potential to be efficacious in a diverse human population. Our study may lead to treatments that protect against
physical deterioration, cognitive decline, and disease susceptibility in the elderly human population.

title: Ribosome biogenesis regulation of neural crest cell differentiation in development and disease
text:
Developmental anomalies affecting the head and face are among the most common birth disorders, and patients
typically undergo extensive surgical, dental, speech and other therapies to restore craniofacial function, spanning
many years and imposing significant psychosocial and financial burdens. This project, through the generation
and analysis of new mutant mice, induced pluripotent stem cell, and zebrafish models to study craniofacial
disorders, will lead to novel discoveries in the fundamental genetic, cellular and molecular mechanisms that are
essential for embryonic development. Results have the potential to guide new preventive therapies and improve
the diagnosis and clinical management of patients.

title: Atlanta Center for Microsystems Engineered Point-of-Care Technologies (ACME POCT)
text:
The mission of the NIH-funded Atlanta Center for Microsystems Engineered POC Technologies (ACME POCT)
is to assist and enable inventors from across the country who have developed microsystems-based POC
technologies in defining their specific clinical needs, conducting clinical validation, and refining their technology,
with the objective of accelerating the path to translation and clinical adoption. The ACME POCT uniquely
leverages Atlanta’s nationally top-ranked clinical programs at Emory University’s hospitals and Children’s
Healthcare of Atlanta, one of the nation’s largest pediatric hospital systems, as well the internationally acclaimed
microsystems engineering expertise at Georgia Tech, which includes the Institute for Electronics and
Nanotechnology, and other one-of-a-kind medical device prototyping, innovation, and testbed facilities. With the
enhanced experience and expertise the ACME POCT gained serving as the Test Validation Core for the Rapid
Acceleration of Diagnostics during the COVID-19 pandemic, the center is now especially well positioned to apply
our lessons learned from RADx towards assisting any and all microsystems POC diagnostics for any and all
clinical applications with a hands-on, pro-active approach.

title: Etiology and pathogenesis of lethal lung developmental disorders in neonates
text:
The main focus of our research is studying the role of SHH-FOXF1 and TBX4-FGF10 signaling pathways in
epithelial-mesenchyme interactions during human lung development as well as in etiology of lethal lung
developmental disorders (LLDD) and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) in neonates. In particular, we are
interested in an interplay between the pathogenic coding variants and the regulatory non-coding regulatory
elements of the FOXF1, FENDRR, TBX4, and FGF10 genes, implied in complex compound inheritance of these
disorders. We hypothesize that (i) non-coding variants are promising therapeutic target and (ii) that a little known
transmembrane protein TMEM100 mediates SHH-FOXF1 and TBX4-FGF10 signaling during human lung
development.

title: The mutational mechanisms shaping melanocytes in human skin
text:
For this grant, we will catalogue the mutational factors shaping melanocytes in normal human skin. Completion
of these studies will address major gaps in knowledge needed to understand the etiology of melanoma, guide
strategies to prevent melanoma, and inform molecular strategies to slow down the evolution of melanoma.
